walkthrough:
A perpendicular bisector must pass through the midpoint at a right angle.
Calculate the midpoint $M$ and gradient $m_{AB}$ of segment $AB$:
$$M = \left(\dfrac{-3 + 5}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 6}{2}\right) = (1, 4)$$
$$m_{AB} = \dfrac{6 - 2}{5 - (-3)} = \dfrac{4}{8} = \dfrac{1}{2} \implies m_{\text{perp}} = -2$$

Form the perpendicular bisector equation through $M(1, 4)$:
$$y - 4 = -2(x - 1)$$
$$y - 4 = -2x + 2 \implies y = -2x + 6$$
